title: iOS 27.2 upgraded Apple Photos in two ways, here’s what’s new
snippet: Apple Photos got a lot of new features in iOS 27, but the recent release of iOS 27.2 brought even more improvements. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Apple Photos got a lot of new features in iOS 27, but the recent release of iOS 27.2 brought even more improvements. Here’s what’s new.

Shared Albums are among my favorite features in the Photos app. I don’t post on social media often, but I love using Shared Albums because they provide a social media-style experience in a private way that lives right inside Photos.

iOS 27 brought a variety of big improvements to Shared Albums. And in iOS 27.2, Apple introduced four more.

Per Apple’s release notes, here’s what’s new:

you can now edit captions for your photos and videos

comments can be edited too

there’s a feature to prevent adding duplicate photos to an album

the app can display a reminder before albums expire, so participants can save photos before they’re gone

To get these new features, you’ll need to make sure your Shared Albums have been upgraded for iOS 27.

#2: SynthID watermarking to identify AI-modified photos

One complication introduced by AI is that it can be hard to know if an image is real or AI-generated. 

This challenge extends to AI-edited photos too, which might have key details changed by tools like iOS 27’s Extend, Reframe, and Clean Up features in Photos.

Apple is tackling the issue with its new Reference Image feature in iPhone 18 Pro, and also through a software enhancement that rolled out in iOS 27.2.

Per Apple, its latest software update adds the following:

Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground

SynthID is a cross-platform standard developed by Google that embeds unnoticeable digital watermarks into AI-modified photos. Users won’t see a visible watermark, but anyone who checks for a SynthID marker will find it.

snippet: iOS 27.3 is currently in beta testing with developers and public beta users. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 … 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. fullText:
iOS 27.3 is currently in beta testing with developers and public beta users. The update includes multiple new features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 …

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

iOS 27.3 release date

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:

December 12, 2025

December 11, 2024

December 11, 2023

December 13, 2022

December 13, 2021

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

iOS 27.3 new features

Redesigned Health app

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

Apple Fitness+

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

Read more: Apple announces Fitness+ Gym Strength program with personalized workout plans

iPhone Duo updates

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords. 

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display. 

Read more: iOS 27.3 introduces new iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use

Read more: iOS 27.3 changes the iPhone Duo keyboard, here’s how

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds new face unlock feature for iPhone Duo

Revamped StandBy

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

Read more: iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s revamped StandBy to other iPhones

New Siri AI features

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

Read more: iOS 27.3 expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps

Read more: Developers can now create advanced ‘app skills’ for Siri AI

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

Siri AI and Apple Intelligence usage limits

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like: 

Siri AI: Complex, multi-step actions 

Photo tools: Clean Up, Extend, Spatial Reframing, and Image Playground

AFM Cloud and Cloud Pro models in Shortcuts

Third-party apps using Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute

You can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ plan, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms. 

Read more: Apple reveals how iCloud+ increases Siri AI and Apple Intelligence usage limits

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds Siri AI usage limits, here’s what counts toward your limit

Apple Intelligence in China

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:

Real-time translation across Messages, FaceTime, Phone, and compatible AirPods

Writing tools

Visual intelligence

Clean Up in Photos

Genmoji

Natural language search in Photos

Memory creation in Photos using any prompt

Priority mail in Apple Mail

Email summaries in Apple Mail

Smart Reply in the Mail and Messages apps

Notification summaries

Priority notifications

Reduce Distractions new Focus Mode

**Audio transcription summary **in the Notes app

Summaries of call transcripts

Siri improvements including Type to Siri, more natural language support, and ability to retain context during a conversation

New Safari features

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a new vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

Read more: iOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 add Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more to Safari

Apple Music

For Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

Read more: iOS 27.3 upgrades Apple Music in two ways, here’s what’s new

Apple TV app changes

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the update introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app. 

Second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a new “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design. 

Read more: iOS 27.3 brings vertical video and video podcasts to Apple TV app

More tidbits

Here are a few other changes in iOS 27.3:

You can now switch between VPNs directly from Control Center, rather than just enable or disable the last one you used.

In the Settings app, there’s a new “Use Global Privacy Control” toggle, but the associated support document isn’t live yet.

In Freeform, there are new tools for custom shape and image generation.

The Calendar app has been redesigned, with controls now located at the bottom. Details here. 

Apple News+ puzzles expand to Australia, French Canada, and the UK. 

Wrap up

What are your favorite new features in iOS 27.3? Have you spotted any other changes in the update? Let us know down in the comments.

fullText:
There’s a familiar interruption that comes with shopping online: you’ve found what you want, you’re ready to check out, and the store asks you to sign in. Was this the account with your usual password? Did you change it last time? Is it easier to reset it again?

Proton Pass is designed to take that friction out of your day. It creates strong, unique passwords, remembers them for you, and fills them in when you log in. But it also handles something a password alone can’t: keeping your real email address out of another retailer’s database.

Sponsored by Proton.

For Black Friday, Proton Pass Plus and Pass Family are both 60% off their regular monthly pricing with a one-year subscription, while Proton Unlimited is 50% off. Pass Plus starts at $1.99 per month, billed annually, making this a good opportunity to get your passwords — and a few other important parts of your digital life — organized.

	

Take a look at Proton’s Black Friday offers, starting at $1.99 per month

Better passwords, less work

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

Proton Pass does that work for you. When you sign up for a website, its password generator can create a strong password that’s completely unique. Save it in your vault, and Proton Pass can fill in your credentials when you return.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

Unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

With unlimited logins and encrypted vaults that sync across devices, Proton Pass lets you keep those details together as you move between your phone and computer.

Proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. This makes it trivially easy to access your passwords, passkeys, and API credentials wherever you find yourself.

Keep your real email address to yourself

Black Friday shopping often leaves something behind long after the packages arrive: a steady stream of promotional emails from stores you barely remember visiting.

Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

An alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

If that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to update all your other accounts.

It’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

A digital safe for the information you always end up searching for

Passwords are only part of what’s worth keeping in a secure, accessible place.

Proton Pass also stores notes, credit card details, and other confidential information in end-to-end encrypted vaults. That makes it useful for the small, everyday moments when you need something sensitive and don’t want to go looking for it.

When you’re booking a flight, saved passport details let you look up the information you need without digging through a drawer halfway through the reservation.

When you’re shopping online, saved card details mean you don’t have to leave the checkout page to find your wallet.

When you’re traveling, keeping a digital copy of an important document within reach gives you a convenient reference while you’re away from home. It doesn’t replace an original document where one is required, but it can save you from searching through scattered files and messages.

Pass Plus also includes a built-in two-factor authenticator, Dark Web Monitoring, and secure link and vault sharing. Those features give you more ways to manage access to your accounts and share sensitive information when you need to.

Three Black Friday offers, depending on what you need

You don’t have to subscribe to Proton’s entire suite to get its password manager. There are separate offers for individuals, households, and anyone looking for a broader set of privacy tools.

title: Google Is Killing the Nest App. Here’s What Comes Next
snippet: Don’t panic: All your devices should transfer over to Google Home fairly seamlessly.
fullText:
Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices. 

																			Corin Cesaric/CNET
												
			
				

If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being retired, and current users will lose access to both next year.

All Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant. 

The change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.” 

			

More from CNET

What’s changing with Nest moving to Google Home

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

Google Nest

Google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app. 

As part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch. 

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

Corin Cesaric/CNET

Google says that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app.

Part of the goal is to give users the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser. 

What’s changing with Google Assistant?

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

Tyler Lacoma/CNET

On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.

With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

How to make sure you’re ready for Google Home and Gemini for Home voice assistant 

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed. 

For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027. 

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

Google

The other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the company starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

Google says Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and users will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information. 

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Josh Edelson/Contributor/Getty Images

Gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google announced earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Users in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now. 

On your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

title: WhatsApp is raising group chat limit to 1,500 participants
snippet: WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

WhatsApp group chats now allows 1,5000 members

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”

Here’s WABetaInfo:

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the update becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company announced four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

title: Hands-on: Baseus’ new PicoGo Pro USB-C charger is clever, cute, and on sale
snippet: USB-C chargers are pretty standardized at this point, but there’s a fun new trend of adding displays to your power brick that I’ve been very much enjoying, and the new PicoGo Pro from Baseus is a great example with three ports, optimized charging, and a cute little character to top it off – and for Black Friday, it’s pretty deeply discounted, too. more…
fullText:
USB-C chargers are pretty standardized at this point, but there’s a fun new trend of adding displays to your power brick that I’ve been very much enjoying, and the new PicoGo Pro from Baseus is a great example with three ports, optimized charging, and a cute little character to top it off – and for Black Friday, it’s pretty deeply discounted, too.

The Baseus PicoGo Pro (AH22) is a 100W, 3-port USB-C charger designed to top off your laptop, phone, and/or tablet, even all at the same time. For anyone who travels often or just has a lot of devices on hand, chargers like this are a must. Having something you don’t have to think twice about when it comes to charging rates is just so nice, and these have come a long way, too.

Using GaN tech, PicoGo Pro is very compact at about 2 inches tall and a little over an inch wide. I remember having single-port chargers that could barely fast-charge my phone that were twice this size just a few years ago. GaN just absolutely rules, and Baseus is using a special version that reduces heat and improves efficiency. 

But the two reasons I really like this charger aren’t strictly to do with GaN.

	

The first is the built-in display. Again, that’s a trend throughout the industry. Anker has several chargers out with built-in displays as the company helped to really make this popular – the Anker Prime 160W brick is really similar to PicoGo Pro (at a higher price), and it’s the only I’ve been using for months before trying out this Baseus model. 

Baseus has a cute little animated character that accompanies your charging, with little eyes when the charger isn’t active and some fun animations to show your charging rate in real-time. Neat! You can “press” the button to move through the UI and even see the specific charging rate of each connected device. You’ll also see that the brick can recognize the device you have plugged in, though Android devices just show a generic “SAMSUNG” or whatever brand you plug in – Anker, again, had a similar set of features in a brick released earlier in 2026, but some of those features were iPhone-only, and that brick was only a 1-port, 45W charger anyway.

But, like that Anker brick, Baseus supports “smart” charging that adjusts to your device. Plugging in a Galaxy Z Fold 8 that was around 65% full, I saw the brick adjust its charging speed to tailor to the phone, initially going up to full speed before settling down around 28W~. You can manually adjust this with “Turbo” or “Gentle” modes, the former maxing out the charging rate and the latter settling in around 15W for a slower charge. That flexibility is great because it means you can adjust the charging rate to what you need in that moment. Full-speed for a quick top-off on a busy day, slower charging overnight to preserve battery health.

Baseus PicoGo Pro at Amazon – Save with code BSAH22PR5

Baseus isn’t doing much new here, though the GaN tech mentioned earlier is enhanced by some architecture and algorithm adjustments the company has made behind the scenes, but it’s a really good implementation.

Beyond that, it’s also priced pretty well.

Baseus PicoGo Pro’s full price is $59.99, but you’ll probably rarely see it there. Technically, today is its launch date, and it’s already down by over 30% at $39.70 for Black Friday. Value-wise, this one is hard to beat.

title: Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, stock up 30%
snippet: Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The company’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains. It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so … more…
fullText:
Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The company’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so …

The ‘resignation’

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The New York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. 

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12. 

Calls for reinstatement

	

Despite putting the company at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, said that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones said: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”

The reinstatement

That changed today, with the company making the announcement in a press release.

Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” 

As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

Stock up 30%+

The company’s stock price jumped by more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also up per Yahoo Finance.

Nvidia shares soared more than 30% Monday morning […] The S&P 500 (^GSPC) rose 4.5% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) jumped more than 1,200 points to recover by 2.5% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) rallied 7%.

title: ‘Galaxy Watch 10’ won’t launch in 2027 as Samsung tries to slow RAMageddon losses
snippet: According to a new report, Samsung’s next “Galaxy Watch 10” won’t be releasing in 2027 with the company moving to a bi-yearly release schedule for its smartwatches. more…
fullText:
According to a new report, Samsung’s next “Galaxy Watch 10” won’t be releasing in 2027 with the company moving to a bi-yearly release schedule for its smartwatches.

ETNews reports that Samsung will not have a new Galaxy Watch model releasing in 2027, a series that would have likely been called “Galaxy Watch 10.” The reason, the report suggests, is that Samsung is “undertaking a structural overhaul to strengthen profitability” (translated) following two quarters in a row of losses in its mobile division. 

Samsung has released a new Galaxy Watch every year since 2018, with 2021’s Galaxy Watch 4 marking the switch to Wear OS. 

The new schedule will apparently see new Galaxy Watch releases every other year, pushing the next release into 2028. The report goes on to mention that Galaxy Watch is part of a “mature phase” of the smartwatch market, and that Galaxy Watch 9 sales “fell short of expectations” likely due in part to its higher price point. 

	

What’s next for Galaxy Watch?

Apparently, Samsung plans new Galaxy Watch software updates next year as well as “enhancement of healthcare features.” The Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker is also expected in 2027, with Dealabs reporting that the tracker will be priced at €79.90 in Europe, a slight price hike over the previous release.

fullText:
Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now. 

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

New design in iOS 27

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it much easier to switch between different cards during the checkout flow on websites and in apps.

In the new design, you can easily swipe between cards on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to view a grid of all your available Apple Pay cards.

The design also makes it easier to see information about individual cards, including rewards, balances, pay later options, and more.

iOS 27 was released to everyone last week. You can update in the Settings app on your iPhone. 

American Express rewards

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that lets you pay with American Express rewards points.

When shopping online or in apps with an American Express card, you’ll see a new “Use Rewards” option alongside your available Membership Rewards points balance. You can apply points to cover all or part of your purchase, right in the Apple Pay checkout flow.

American Express points redeemed via Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents each. For example, this means 10,000 points can be redeemed for $70 applied towards your purchase.

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a new “Tap to Share” feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

This feature is an extension of Tap to Pay on iPhone. Apple explains:

With just a tap, customers can connect to a participating merchant’s iPhone for a more personalized and faster in-store purchase experience that allows for secure sharing of information, such as email and other contact information, shipping address, loyalty rewards information, and more.

Customers will also be able to view the items in their basket in real time so they can keep track of what they’ve purchased and ensure all sales and discounts are properly applied.

When done, shoppers can complete the checkout on their iPhone using Apple Pay.

Reload debit cards

iPhone users with select banks can manage their debit card balances directly in the Apple Pay interface. According to Apple, you’ll be able to use Apple Pay to add money to a supported debit card directly in Apple Wallet or when checking out.

Bonus: Apple Pay at Walmart 

This one isn’t really a new feature developed by Apple. Instead, it’s something that should’ve happened years ago finally coming to fruition. Walmart has announced that it is finally starting to roll out support for Apple Pay. Apple Pay is also rolling out to Sam’s Club as part of this initiative.  

As of November, Walmart’s roll out of Apple Pay across the United States is complete. 

Wrap up

As Apple Pay continues to increase in popularity and prevalence among retailers, it’s great to see Apple continue to improve the experience. Personally, Apple Pay is my checkout payment method of choice basically everywhere I shop — whether that’s online or in store.

How often do you use Apple Pay? What are your favorite Apple Pay features? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday sale brings big savings on under-sink, countertop, and whole-home systems
snippet: Black Friday is one of the best times of the year to tackle some of the bigger upgrades around your...
fullText:
Black Friday is one of the best times of the year to tackle some of the bigger upgrades around your home, and a better water filtration setup can make a pretty noticeable difference in everyday use. If you’ve been thinking about moving to a more capable reverse osmosis system for drinking, cooking, coffee, tea, and more, Waterdrop Filter has a wide range of its under-sink and countertop models discounted as part of its Black Friday and Cyber Monday Deals.

The sale is now live and runs through November 30, with savings of up to 37% on pretty much everything from higher-capacity under-sink systems for larger households to compact countertop models that are easier to work into smaller kitchens or apartments. That gives you a few different options depending on how much filtered water you need, how much space you have, and how involved you want the setup to be. Head below for a closer look at some of the standout Waterdrop deals.

Waterdrop X12 is a smart premium under-sink option for larger households

One of the more notable deals in the sale is on the Waterdrop X12 Reverse Osmosis System, which is now down to $899 shipped from its usual $1,299 price. That’s a solid $400 discount on one of Waterdrop’s premium under-sink models, and you can use promo code 9TO5GBF26 to save an extra 5% off this RO system, which is built with larger households in mind thanks to its high-capacity 1,200 GPD output. It’s a particularly good fit for families that go through plenty of filtered water throughout the day for drinking, cooking, making beverages, and so on.

The X12 uses an 11-stage reverse osmosis filtration system that helps reduce TDS, chlorine, heavy metals, PFOA, PFOS, and other specified contaminants. It also adds minerals such as calcium and magnesium back into the water through alkaline remineralization, delivering a smoother, more balanced taste for everyday use. With that 1,200 GPD capacity, it can keep up with heavier day-to-day use as well as busier holiday hosting without slowing things down.

	

You’re also getting a tankless design with a 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio, along with a smart faucet that comes in silver, black, bronze, and gold finishes to better match different kitchen setups. The X12 is certified to NSF/ANSI 42, 58, and 372 standards, and it has picked up some notable recognition too, including being named “Best Smart Reverse Osmosis Water System” by Forbes Vetted in 2026 and appearing in The New York Times Wirecutter’s roundup of the best reverse osmosis systems.

The X12 is easily one of the standout options in Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday lineup, and it’s worth considering if you’re looking for a long-term under sink reverse osmosis upgrade and want strong flow, advanced filtration, and plenty of everyday convenience.

Get the Waterdrop X12 RO System for $899 (Reg. $1,299)

Use promo code 9TO5GBF26 for extra 5% off

G6A6 brings under-sink RO to smaller kitchens for under $200

You don’t necessarily need a huge kitchen or a large family to make the jump to a proper RO setup, and that’s where the latest Waterdrop G6A6 Reverse Osmosis System comes in. This compact model is down to $189.99 shipped from its $300 usual price for Black Friday, and you use promo code 9TO5GBF26 to score an extra 5% off, making it one of the more affordable options in Waterdrop Filter’s under-sink lineup this year. It’s designed with smaller households and tighter kitchens in mind, while still offering a 600 GPD capacity that should comfortably handle everyday drinking, cooking, and beverage needs.

The biggest advantage of the G6A6 system is its compact design, which Waterdrop says can save up to 81.8% of under-sink space. That makes it a particularly good fit for apartments, smaller kitchens, or any setup where you don’t want a bulky filtration system taking up most of the cabinet.

Despite the smaller footprint, though, this model can delivers up to 600 gallons per day, which should be more than enough for the everyday drinking, cooking, and beverage needs of a smaller household. Its eight-stage filtration system is also paired with alkaline remineralization to add minerals such as calcium and magnesium back for a better-tasting water.

It’s safe to say the Waterdrop G6A6 is probably the more sensible pick over stepping up to something as powerful as the X12 if you have a smaller family of three or four, or you’re simply working with limited kitchen space.

Get the Waterdrop G6A6 RO system for $189.99 (Reg. $300)

Use promo code 9TO5GBF26 for extra 5% off

M6HG gives you filtered hot water without any installation

If you’d rather skip an under-sink installation altogether, the Waterdrop M6HG Mineral Instant Hot Reverse Osmosis System is another solid option in the sale. This newer 2026 countertop model is down to $299 shipped from its usual $429 price right now, and the promo code 9TO5GBF26 gets you an extra 5% off for additional savings. This particular model gives you filtered water plus instant heating in one compact setup without any plumbing required.

That instant-heating setup makes the M6HG a particularly solid pick as we’re heading into the colder months. It can dispense filtered water anywhere from room temperature up to 95°C, or 203°F, in seconds, which means you can jump straight into making coffee, tea, breakfast, or other hot drinks without waiting around for a kettle.

It also uses an eight-stage RO filtration system to help reduce TDS, chlorine, fluoride, PFAS, heavy metals, unpleasant odors, and other specified substances. Waterdrop then adds minerals such as calcium and magnesium back into the water through remineralization, similar to the X12 and G6A6 models highlighted above.

The Waterdrop M6HG also comes with a detachable 1.2-liter glass pitcher, which makes it a bit easier to carry filtered water over to the dining table, coffee station, or wherever else you need it. There’s no permanent installation required either, so you can simply place the unit on the counter and get going. That makes it a particularly convenient option for renters, apartments, home offices, RVs, or anyone who wants a countertop reverse osmosis system without having to make any changes to the plumbing.

Get the Waterdrop M6HG Mineral Instant Hot RO System for $299 (Reg. $429)

Use promo code 9TO5GBF26 for extra 5% off

CT01 is the more affordable way to get hot and cold filtered water

The Waterdrop CT01 Hot & Cold Water Filter Dispenser is another countertop option worth checking out from the sale, especially if you don’t need a full reverse osmosis setup. It’s down to $199.99 shipped for Black Friday with a 20% discount, and the promo code 9TO5GBF26 for an extra 5% off makes it one of the more affordable ways to add filtered hot and cold water to your kitchen or workspace.

The CT01 can dispense water anywhere from 59°F to 203°F, covering everything from a cold glass of water to oatmeal, coffee, tea, and other hot drinks without the need for a separate kettle. It’s geared more toward everyday convenience than advanced RO filtration, so it works particularly well for apartments, offices, students, couples, or anyone who wants a simple all-in-one countertop setup.

It offers a six-stage filtration system to help reduce chlorine, rust, sediment, and other common impurities while retaining beneficial minerals in the water. Its 1.32-gallon capacity also helps cut down on frequent refills throughout the day, and there’s no wastewater or installation to deal with either. That keeps the whole setup fairly simple if you just want filtered hot and cold water without adding a more involved system to your kitchen.

Get the Waterdrop CT01 Instant Hot & Cold Water Filter Dispenser for $199.99

Use promo code 9TO5GBF26 for extra 5% off

WHF3E-SKH takes filtration beyond the kitchen

Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday lineup also includes a deal on its WHF3E-SKH Whole-House Water Filtration System, which is down to $369.99 shipped from its usual $530 price. Be sure to enter promo code 9TO5GBF26 to score an additional 5% off. This one is built specifically for homes that rely on well water, with filtration happening before the water gets distributed throughout the house. The WHF3E-SKH system uses a nine-layer filtration setup to help reduce scale, chlorine, lead, unpleasant tastes, odors, and other impurities before the water reaches your faucets, showers, appliances, and other fixtures.

It supports flow rates of up to 15 gallons per minute, giving it enough capacity to keep up with busier households running showers, laundry, cooking, and cleaning at the same time. Waterdrop also rates the system for up to 250,000 gallons, or around one year of filtration, depending on usage and water conditions.

You can also pair the WHF3E-SKH with one of Waterdrop’s RO systems for a more complete setup, using the whole-house filter to handle water throughout the home while the RO system takes care of drinking and cooking water at the kitchen sink.

As far as the main filtration systems are concerned, the X12 is a premium pick for larger households that need higher capacity, while the G6A6 offers a much more compact and affordable under-sink alternative for smaller kitchens. title: Google Meet unlocks 1080p video streaming for all accounts on web
snippet: Streaming in 1080p will be the default in Google Meet, regardless of whether you pay for Google Workspace. That includes personal Google Accounts. more…
fullText:
Streaming in 1080p will be the default in Google Meet, regardless of whether you pay for Google Workspace. That includes personal Google Accounts.

Google says users will default to sending and receiving 1080p video, at the minimum. Previously, Google Meet made 720p the standard for streaming, and a higher resolution had historically been locked behind the Google One 2TB plan. That’s been true since 1080p streaming was rolled out in 2023.

The upgrade will roll out to everyone, including those with Google Workspace accounts and personal Google Accounts. The only requirement to stream your own 1080p video in Google Meet for web will be hardware-based. Google’s press release states that devices with cameras capable of streaming in high definition will do so, and the feature will be turned on automatically.

It can be disabled, though. Users can head to Settings > Video in Google Meet for web. Video will also appear in a lower resolution if the user’s video tile is shrunk down on-screen.

	

The update appears to be centered on web-only instances of Google Meet, and might not include the app on Android or iOS. For the time being, those versions may still be limited to streaming in 720p for those who don’t have an active Google One subscription.

Google Meet started its extended rollout of 1080p streaming to everyone earlier this month, so it shouldn’t be much longer until the change has taken place completely.

title: MacBook Neo 2 likely to launch around March, could feature new colors: report
snippet: One of Apple’s most beloved products this year was undoubtedly the MacBook Neo. Unlike some of its other budget products, Apple seems interested in updating the MacBook Neo on an annual cycle, and we may get the next MacBook Neo around March. more…
fullText:
One of Apple’s most beloved products this year was undoubtedly the MacBook Neo. Unlike some of its other budget products, Apple seems interested in updating the MacBook Neo on an annual cycle, and we may get the next MacBook Neo around March.

Apple targeting iOS 27.4 cycle for new budget products

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is targeting the iOS/macOS 27.4 release cycle for the release of the new MacBook Neo, as well as the A19 budget iPad, iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and OLED iPad Air.

While he notes that this cycle runs between February and March, it doesn’t necessarily mean the products will launch on the earlier end of that spectrum. Apple is also expected to release the iPhone Air 2, OLED iPad Air, and a new iPad Pro within the first half of the year, but they’ll likely come a bit later than the aforementioned products.

MacBook Neo 2 upgrades

As expected, the next MacBook Neo will bump up from the A18 Pro chip with 8GB of RAM to the A19 Pro chip with 12GB of RAM.

Apple will also introduce new colors on the MacBook Neo “frequently,” though it’s unclear if we’ll see that with the next iteration. From the Power On newsletter:

The other thing I’ve heard is that Apple plans to refresh the MacBook Neo’s colors frequently. We’ll see if that trend starts with the first follow-up.

Wrap up

I’m certainly excited to see the next generation MacBook Neo, especially with 12GB of unified memory. While 8GB is certainly fine, heavy multitaskers will notice it, especially with unoptimized software.

The bigger question is: will the next MacBook Neo have a price increase? With additional RAM included, it feels inevitable. 

	

Apple increased the price of MacBook Neo from $599 to $699 back in June, and in October the company also silently decreased the education discount by $50, meaning the education price has increased from $499 to $649 since launch.

If there is a price increase, it likely won’t be too major, maybe $50 – leaving the computer at $749. Compared to the rest of the laptop landscape, MacBook Neo would still be a good value. We’ll see what happens.

snippet: Recently, UGREEN introduced a new Qi2.2 25W 10000mAh MagSafe battery bank for iPhone. There have been plenty of these, but this one has an interesting new twist: liquid cooling. For Black Friday, it’s on sale for 40% off, making it more affordable than ever. more…
fullText:
Recently, UGREEN introduced a new Qi2.2 25W 10000mAh MagSafe battery bank for iPhone. There have been plenty of these, but this one has an interesting new twist: liquid cooling. For Black Friday, it’s on sale for 40% off, making it more affordable than ever.

On the back of the battery, there’s a window that showcases the liquid within the battery bank moving throughout it. This should help keep it a little bit cooler than most MagSafe battery banks.

UGREEN says that it’ll be around 18 degrees cooler than usual, and while that’s probably true – it’s worth nothing that it still isn’t a cold battery bank, it’s just cooler than usual. It’ll still feel warm in your hand.

On the bottom of the battery bank, UGREEN integrates a USB-C cable for charging your phone or any other USB-C device that can’t (or you prefer not to) charge wirelessly. I found it a bit handy at times, since of course wireless charging is never as energy efficient as wired charging.

I will admit, the battery bank is a little bit thick, and the lack of a kickstand is somewhat bothersome at this price point, especially when so many others offer one. That said, if heat is a concern of yours with MagSafe battery banks, this one will definitely solve that for you.

On the side, it offers a small display for showing battery percentage and charging speed.

One last thing of note: if you’re buying an iPhone Duo, this will stick out from the bottom of the phone. This is true for most MagSafe accessories on iPhone Duo, though.

title: Honor just supercharged its smartwatch lineup with a new Pro model
snippet: The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks. more…
fullText:
The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks.

In the world of athletic smartwatches, it isn’t often that you could mistake one for a luxury watch, but Honor seems to want to flip all that on its head with the Honor Watch 6 Pro. Just take a look at this excerpt from the company’s press release:

Framing this brilliant display is a Precision Nanocrystalline Ceramic bezel crafted through a 1400°C high-temperature integrated sintering process, delivering a delicate texture and rich visual depth.

Inspired by modernist architecture, its diamond-cut octagonal rotatable crown features a dual-layer horizontal and vertical cut, complemented by a side button for intuitive navigation.

That sounds pretty wild to me, and it’s backed up by specs that sound just as legit, too. On top is a 1.5-inch LTPO Tandem AMOLED display that outputs 5,500-nit peak brightness. Underneath is a bevy of new sensors called the Intelligent Sense System, which Honor says combines “multi-wavelength monitoring, multi-optical path patrol technology, and anti-interference glass technology to reach deep skin layers.”

Pre-sales begin today at €279/£229 for early bird pricing.

Runners will be pleased to know that the Honor Watch 6 Pro not only incorporates a dual-band GPS, but combines it with a “star-pointing 3-antenna design” and an AI fusion algorithm, which should deliver ultra-accurate tracking in any location and no matter how you hold your wrist. Despite its luxury looks, this one tracks over 120 sports modes, including Honor’s Professional Running Coach feature, which tracks running posture, lactate threshold, heart rate targets, and keeps you on pace with real-time voice coaching.

	

During sports modes like Badminton, the watch can identify more than six types of swings, and Honor says other sports modes can deliver similarly detailed statistics. The watch is 5ATM, IP68, IP69, and IP69K water-and-dust-resistant rated, plus it integrates directly with Strava so you can pull all your fitness data together.

Honor is incorporating a new wrist twist gesture system this time around, letting you use gestures to perform actions hands-free. The watch is rated at 10 days of battery life on a single charge in regular usage mode, while endurance mode will stretch that to 18 days. Pre-sales begin today, November 19, and run until December 31, when the watch is expected to launch, starting at €279/£229 for early bird pricing. After launch, the retail MSRP starts at €379/£329.

fullText:
Stevie Bonifield

 

is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Mozilla released Firefox 161 on Tuesday with a new setting you can use to choose which pages automatically open with the browser’s VPN active. Using the “Manage VPN rules” option in Firefox’s VPN panel, you can set it to “always on” or “always off” for specific sites, so you don’t have to toggle it manually every time you visit certain pages.

Starting Tuesday, Mozilla is also rolling out a “Fire” button in standard Firefox windows that lets you quickly clear your browsing data directly from the toolbar. You can choose which data it deletes, including browsing history, downloads history, cookie data, site data, temporary files, saved form info, and website permissions and preferences. If you set the button to delete all of that data, clicking it will sign you out of everything and open a fresh Firefox window.

Tuesday’s Firefox update also adds an option for creating a keyboard shortcut for copying your current tab’s URL, and brings its “read aloud” option in Reader Mode to the Android version of Firefox. Alongside the update, Mozilla says Firefox is also now available directly through the Play Store on cars with Google built-in.

This year, Waterdrop has everything from premium reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration for a house full of holiday guests to budget-friendly, installation-free setups for cozy apartment evenings. And the best part? No matter which you pick, you’re on your way to better-tasting water for drinking, cooking, and those extra demands that come with holiday hosting — complete with some exclusive 9to5Google discounts.

Waterdrop’s X16 is perfect for a big household that keeps the faucet busy

If your kitchen transforms into your home’s central hangout spot whenever guests are around, the Waterdrop X16 Reverse Osmosis System makes a strong case for going premium. Its 1,600-gallon-per-day rated capacity is the highest of the under-sink models here, perfect for a kitchen where glasses, pitchers, pots, and mugs are filled constantly throughout the day.

	

The X16 RO System is as powerful as that capacity makes it sound. It features Waterdrop’s excellent 11-stage reverse osmosis filter, which traps and removes debris, contaminants, and everything else you don’t want in your water, while its alkaline remineralization process restores that much-needed calcium and magnesium your body needs. Its compact, tankless design tucks neatly under your kitchen sink, while a digital faucet shows water and filter information and lets you select the exact amount of water you want to dispense.

The X16 also features IAPMO certification to NSF/ANSI 42 and 58 for specified performance claims, plus NSF/ANSI 372 for lead content in the parts that contact water. You don’t just have to take its word, though: Wired called the Waterdrop Filter X16 the “Rolls-Royce of water filtration.” The cleanest, clearest water available, ready for your refreshment every day of the year.

The X16 usually costs $1,999, but Black Friday pricing knocks 35% off to bring it down to $1,299. This year, you can use promo code 9TO5GBF26 to take another 5% off the sale price, bringing your final cost down to $1,234. Those are some incredible savings over the X16’s typical list price, and considering its faster flow and dispensing controls over competing models, it’s one of those rare Black Friday purchases you’ll feel great about for years to come.

Waterdrop’s G3P800 and G5P500A deliver premium under-sink filtration at a price you’ll love

Under-sink reverse osmosis doesn’t have to break the bank. For a family that wants a smart faucet and plenty of filtered water ready for cooking, coffee, and everyday drinking, the Waterdrop G3P800 Reverse Osmosis System is absolutely the model for you to consider this Black Friday.

The G3P800 RO System features an 800-gallon-per-day rating, 10-stage filtration, UV treatment, a tankless design, and a 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio. Those are well beyond basic specs for water filtration, but at a price you can feel good about. And since the G3P800 is certified to NSF/ANSI 42, 53, 58, and 372 standards, you can rest assured that every sip features reduced chlorine, lead, PFOA, and PFOS. 

Waterdrop has the G3P800 RO System marked down 30% for Black Friday, bringing the price to just $699, but 9to5Google readers can use code 9TO5GBF26 to another 5% off for a grand total of just $664.

If you’re just getting started with reverse osmosis water filtration — or maybe you’re looking to introduce your friends or family to the benefits of cleaner hydration — the Waterdrop G5P500A Reverse Osmosis System might be the best fit this holiday season. It keeps the tankless setup from the G3P800, combining it with a smaller 500-gallon-per-day rated capacity, eight-stage filtration, and alkaline remineralization. While you do lose out on the G3P800’s smart faucet and UV treatment, the price point here simply cannot be beat.

At $190 — down 23% from its $259.99 MSRP, plus 9to5Google’s additional 5% discount — the G5P500A RO System gives you under-sink reverse osmosis without making a premium faucet part of the purchase. After all, the best water filter is the one with the features you’ll actually put to good use, and for a smaller household, this model still goes well beyond the everyday basics.

If you prefer to keep your filtration on the counter, Waterdrop’s M6CG and C2SL deliver easy, pitcher-ready water

If under-sink installation isn’t an option for your home, Waterdrop Filter has two very different answers, both new to its lineup in 2026. Each brings countertop-based reverse osmosis to apartments, offices, and smaller kitchens, and they’re perfect for newlyweds, students, and more. Your choice comes down to whether you want hot and cold water ready and on-demand, or a pitcher you can keep filled in the fridge for perfectly chilled water whenever you want it.

The Waterdrop M6CG Mineral Hot & Cold Reverse Osmosis System dispenses mineralized water from 59°F to 203°F. That means that, from sunup to sundown, morning coffee to that midnight glass of water, you’re drinking clean, crisp, filtered water. The M6CG features five volume presets for one-touch refills, a detachable 40-ounce glass pitcher for serving guests, and a customizable Favorites mode for that perfect cup. Plus, separate clean-water and wastewater tanks and a 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio prevent backflow pollution and extend your filter’s lifespan.

If you’re someone who’ll use hot and cold water regularly, the Waterdrop M6CG RO System is a no-brainer. You can pick it up for just $390 after promo code 9TO5GBF26, way below its typical $539 list price.

If you don’t need the temperature controls, the Waterdrop C2SL Mineral Reverse Osmosis System keeps things simpler and costs much less. It pairs seven-stage filtration with the company’s remineralization process, and the unit automatically refills a detachable 40-ounce glass pitcher that you can keep in your fridge. For one or two people who want countertop reverse osmosis without a headache-inducing plumbing project, it’s an easy way to keep better-tasting water always ready to pour.

The C2SL RO System can be yours for just $133 after a 22% discount from its $179.99 list price and with 9to5Google’s promo code, 9TO5GBF26.

This Black Friday, get the cleaner water you’ve been waiting for

A Waterdrop reverse osmosis system can make sense at any of these price points. The X16 is for the household that will put its speed and controls to work. The G3P800 keeps smart features at a lower price. The G5P500A makes under-sink RO more affordable than ever. And for those with limited space, countertop models let you decide how much hot-and-cold convenience you want without ever touching your home’s plumbing system. Whichever fits your routine, don’t wait — Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday offers run through November 30th.

title: Huang reportedly admitted to more than two affairs to Nvidia’s board
snippet: During a meeting before his reinstatement, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

5:29 AM PST · November 24, 2026

Image Credits:Haje Jan Kamps / TechCrunch

		

							

											
									

					

	

In a complete U-turn, Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as the CEO and president of the chipmaker, just a fortnight after he resigned. 

During a meeting before his reinstatement, however, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Early in November, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair in a letter to employees. At the time, he was ostensibly talking about his relationship with Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (not related to Jensen). Later, it was reported that he’d also had a relationship with Nvidia’s VP of health, Kimberly Powell.

Afterwards, Reuters reported that he also had an affair with another employee.

It’s not clear which affairs Huang admitted to during this recent conversation with Nvidia’s board of directors.

Huang’s return was spurred by a personal intervention from the U.S. government, Nvidia’s board said in a statement on Monday, and President Donald Trump apparently called the board to bat for Huang’s reinstatement. 

The Wall Street Journal reports that over the weekend, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance that the Justice Department wasn’t investigating Huang and there was no evidence that he was a national security risk, after which both contacted the company’s board.

Huang received a “hero’s welcome” at Nvidia’s HQ, with several employees applauding his return.

title: The Best Foldable Phones to Give This Holiday Season
snippet: For the tech enthusiast in your life, a foldable phone could be an interesting alternative to a traditional smartphone. We’ve rounded up our top picks, from book-style designs to flip phones.
fullText:
If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over. 

After reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-new device? (You’ve been warned.) 

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

		

			

iPhone Duo: Great for the Apple fan in your life

The iPhone Duo has a 5.4-inch cover display with a Ceramic Shield 2 covering to protect against scratches.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays. 

The compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

The Duo is a great gift for someone who’s said they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV shows on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use. 

The iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch matte inner display to reduce glare.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity. 

The Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos. 

Multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them. 

Perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.  

Galaxy Z Fold 8: Best foldable for Android lovers

Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is compact and versatile.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

For the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.)

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

It’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

The Z Fold 8 has a tablet-like 7.6-inch inner display.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job. 

The Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

Motorola Razr 2026: A flip phone for nostalgists

The 2026 Motorola Razr has a 3.6-inch cover display that’s good for quickly checking apps.David Lumb/CNET

Some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr. 

The phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

For most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography. 

The Motorola Razr 2026’s inner screen is 6.9 inches.David Lumb/CNET

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference. 

The Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr. 

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

title: Jensen Huang scheduled to testify next week in Senate following reinstatement as Nvidia CEO
snippet: The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about the affair with the suspected Chinese spy.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

10:12 AM PST · November 23, 2026

Image Credits:Fabrice COFFRINI/AFP / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, according to a notice on the committee’s website. 

The development comes just hours after Huang was reinstated as Nvidia chief executive, less than two weeks following his resignation after it was revealed that he engaged in at least two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected by the U.S. government of working as a Chinese spy.

The Senate Banking Committee has jurisdiction over export control policies that are designed to prevent sensitive U.S. technologies, such as chips capable of powering AI models, from falling into the hands of foreign governments and militaries.

The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about his affair with the suspected Chinese spy and his potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations.

It’s worth noting that before his reinstatement as CEO, Huang had already agreed to appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee on December 1.

Among iOS 27’s many new features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets dual iPhone users keep the same phone number across devices

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the update also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:

After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

	

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple plans to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

Do you have a need to use the same phone number on multiple iPhones? For what reason? Let us know in the comments.

fullText:
AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade.

Apple doubled Active Noise Cancellation in AirPods Pro 3, and it’s been a huge upgrade

I’ve been using AirPods Pro 3 for over a year, and they had a lot to live up to because I already loved AirPods Pro 2 so much. Initially I found the new ear tips less comfortable, but thankfully that issue went away after a little extra time.

Some highlights of AirPods Pro 3 include the longer battery life, with 8 hours per charge compared to 6 on the previous model. The charging case’s new Ultra Wideband chip also makes it easier to find when it’s lost. Some users will appreciate the heart rate sensor, but I wear an Apple Watch all the time so it doesn’t benefit me much.

These new features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple says it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:

removes up to 2x more noise than AirPods Pro 2

removes up to 4x more noise than AirPods Pro

I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

One reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is important to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.

title: Lenovo Legion Go Beam leaks with Android instead of SteamOS
snippet: The variety of gaming handhelds from Lenovo is about to get larger. Leaked details suggest the Lenovo Legion Go Beam will run Android instead of SteamOS on a high-refresh display. more…
fullText:
The variety of gaming handhelds from Lenovo is about to get larger. Leaked details suggest the Lenovo Legion Go Beam will run Android instead of SteamOS on a high-refresh display.

Lenovo is sticking with the Legion Go branding to offer something a little different to users. Instead of a SteamOS or Windows device, the Legion Go Beam is said to run Android (via Windows Latest). Specifically, Android 16.

That doesn’t limit it to Android titles alone. Android happens to make the perfect platform for cloud game streaming. Services like GeForce Now, Xbox Game Pass, and more offer a comparable experience to what a PC does for a fixed subscription, and that’s without the hardware internals something like the Legion Go 2 would need to run games natively.

The leak also notes the Lenovo Legion Go Beam will have a 7-inch 120Hz display, though there’s no information on what resolution or panel type the handheld might have. It’s likely 1080p or higher, though a lower resolution obviously will net users better performance. Battery is up in the air, too, other than a standard “long-lasting battery life” claim attributed to Lenovo.

	

This handheld takes a lot from the Legion Go 2 in design, as it should. It’s a comfortable device, and this shouldn’t be any different. It lacks a trackpad in favor of a traditional controller layout. It also has standard ports like one USB-C and 3.5mm headphone jack.

Pricing is a mystery. Devices like the Logitech G Cloud were such a hit because they delivered the needed performance at a good price. But those handhelds had a lower refresh rate. Still, hoping for a price tag around $350 or less isn’t such a bad thing.
